Tosafot on Bava Batra 45b:1:1.hebrew: המפקיד אצל חבירו בעדים צריך להחזיר לו בעדים - וא"ת: אכתי להימניה במיגו דאי בעי אמר נאנסו, כדאמרינן בסוף המוכר את הבית (לקמן בבא בתרא דף ע. ושם) גבי מפקיד אצל חבירו בשטר; ואפי' מאן דפליג התם, היינו משום דשטרך בידי מאי בעי? ותירץ ר"ת: דודאי הוה מצי אביי למיפרך ליה "אי הכי, בעדים נמי להימניה במיגו דאי בעי אמר נאנסו", אלא דלא אסיק אדעתיה, ואותביה מברייתא, ואודי ליה דבראה איירי מתני', ותו ליכא למפרך מידי אנאנסו. וי"מ דהא דקאמר הכא דצריך להחזיר לו בעדים, היינו אם רוצה להיות פטור משבועה; אבל בשבועה נאמן במיגו דנאנסו, ואין מחזיר לו בעדים. והכי פי' לעיל: "לא שנו" — דאומן אין לו חזקה בלא שבועה אלא שמסר לו בעדים, אבל מסר לו שלא בעדים נאמן בלא שבועה במיגו דאי בעי אמר לא היו דברים מעולם. ומיירי קודם שנתקנה שבועת היסת, ולכך כי אמר לא היו דברים מעולם אין צריך שבועה; אי נמי לאחר שנתקנה, וללישנא דבעי בשבועה דררא דממונא, ולא חשיב הכא דררא דממונא, דאמר לא בא לידי בתורת אומנות ואין מודה שנתחייב בו מעולם, ולא חשיב דררא דממונא אלא מנה לי בידך, וא"ל הן, למחר א"ל תנהו לי, וא"ל נתתיו לך, שמודה שנתחייב. ועל פירוש זה קשה לר"ח: דמאי פריך לקמן "מראה עבדו ביד אומן, אי דאיכא עדים למה לי ראה, לייתי עדים ולישקול"? הא מהני ראה, דאפילו בשבועה לא יהא נאמן, דאין לו מיגו דבלא ראה מהימן הוא בשבועה במיגו דנאנסו! וברייתא משמע דלא אמר כלום, דאפילו בשבועה אינו נאמן. ונראה לו לתרץ דהכא לא חשיב מיגו, דטעמא דמ"ד דצריך להחזיר בעדים משום דכיון דלא הימניה בשבועה, כדאמר בשבועות (דף מא: ושם), דהויא כאילו א"ל בהדיא "אל תחזיר לי אלא בעדים", הלכך לא מהימן במיגו דאיהו דאפסיד אנפשיה. אבל התם בהמוכר, סבר דאין צריך להחזיר לו בעדים, ולא חשיב כאילו אמר "אל תחזירני אלא בעדים", ולכך נאמן במיגו. אבל אין נראה, דאפילו מאן דאית ליה צריך להחזיר לו בעדים, כי איכא מיגו מהימן; דאי לאו הכי, תקשי: מאי פריך ליה אביי מההיא דראה עבדו ביד אומן, דסברא דאין צריך להחזיר לו בעדים? הא איכא תנא בשבועות דאית ליה "המלוה את חבירו בעדים צריך להחזיר לו בעדים", ויסבור רבה כוותיה! אלא משום דאפילו ההוא תנא דשבועות מודה בפקדון דאיכא מיגו דנאנסו, דאין צריך להחזיר לו בעדים — לכך נראה כפי' ר"ת:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 45b:1:1.english: "One who deposits [an item] with his fellow in the presence of witnesses must return it to him in the presence of witnesses" - And if you ask: Still, let him be believed because of a migo, [namely] that had he wished, he could have said "it was lost through circumstances beyond my control (ones)," as we say at the end of [the chapter] "HaMokher et HaBayit" (below, Bava Batra 70a, there) regarding one who deposits with his fellow [in the presence of] a document; and even the one who disagrees there, [it is] only because [the bailee can say,] "Your document is in my hands — what does he want?" And Rabbeinu Tam answered: Certainly Abaye could have challenged him, [saying,] "If so, [in the case of] witnesses too, let him be believed because of a migo that had he wished, he could have said 'it was lost through ones'," except that it did not occur to him, and he raised an objection against him from a baraita, and [Rabbah] conceded to him that the Mishnah is dealing with [a case where the bailee] saw [the item in the claimant's possession]; and there is nothing further to challenge regarding [the claim of] ones. And some explain that what [Rabbah] says here, that he must return it to him in the presence of witnesses, means [this is] if he wants to be exempt from an oath; but with an oath he is believed because of the migo of [claiming] ones, and he does not [need to] return it to him in the presence of witnesses. And so they explain [Rabbah's statement] earlier: "They only taught [this]" — that a craftsman has no presumption [of having returned the item] without an oath only where [the owner] handed it over to him in the presence of witnesses; but if he handed it over to him not in the presence of witnesses, he is believed without an oath, because of a migo that had he wished, he could have said "there were never any dealings between us." And [this] is speaking of the period before the heset oath was enacted, and therefore when he says "there were never any dealings," he does not need an oath; or alternatively, [it is speaking of the period] after it was enacted, and according to the version [of the text] that [the oath is required] only where there is a derara demamona (a definite monetary claim), and here it is not considered a derara demamona, since [the craftsman] says, "It never came into my hands as a craftsman," and he does not admit that he was ever obligated for it. And it is considered a derara demamona only [in a case such as]: "I have a maneh [owed to me] by you," and [the other] said to him, "Yes," [and] the next day [the claimant] said to him, "Give it to me," and he said to him, "I already gave it to you," [in which case] he admits that he was obligated. And against this explanation, Rabbeinu Chaim objects: For what does [the Gemara] challenge below from [the case of one who] "saw his slave in the hands of a craftsman": "If there are witnesses, why do I need [the clause] 'he saw'? Let him bring witnesses and take [it]"? [But] "he saw" is useful, for [the craftsman] would not be believed even with an oath, because he has no migo [in a case where the owner saw], whereas without [the owner] having seen, he is believed with an oath because of the migo of [claiming] ones! And the baraita implies that [the craftsman] says nothing [of value], for he is not believed even with an oath. And it seems to him [that one should] resolve [this by saying] that here it is not considered a migo, for the reasoning of the one who holds that one must return [the deposit] in the presence of witnesses is that since [the depositor] did not trust him with an oath, as it says in Shevuot (41b, there), it is as if he had said to him explicitly, "Do not return it to me except in the presence of witnesses"; therefore he is not believed through a migo, since he himself caused the loss to himself. But there, [in the case of] the seller, [the depositor] holds that one need not return it to him in the presence of witnesses, and it is not considered as if he had said, "Do not return it to me except in the presence of witnesses," and therefore he is believed through a migo. But this does not seem right, [because] even the one who holds that one must return it to him in the presence of witnesses, when there is a migo, he is believed; for if not so, one could raise a difficulty: Why does Abaye challenge him from that [case] of "saw his slave in the hands of a craftsman," on the reasoning that one need not return it to him in the presence of witnesses? Surely there is a Tanna in Shevuot who holds that "one who lends to his fellow in the presence of witnesses must repay him in the presence of witnesses," and Rabbah could hold like him! Rather, [it must be] because even that Tanna of Shevuot concedes, regarding a deposit where there is a migo of [claiming] ones, that one need not return it to him in the presence of witnesses; therefore, the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam seems [correct]:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 45b:8:1.hebrew: נתנה לו בזמנו נשבע ונוטל - וא"ת: והא אמר בפ' המקבל (ב"מ דף קיב: ושם): אומן אומר "שתים קצצת לי", והלה אומר "לא קצצתי לך אלא אחת" — המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה, דקציצה מידע ידיע! ובפ' כל הנשבעין (שבועות דף מו. ושם) פריך ליה, ומשני: דהך דהכא כרבי יהודה, דקציצה נמי לא דכיר, דטרוד הוא בפועליו. וא"ת: א"כ לאחר זמנו נמי, אמאי אמר המע"ה? הוה לן למימר נשבע ונוטל! דמאי טעמא אמרינן בעלמא לאחר זמנו דאין נשבע ונוטל, כדמפרש בריש כל הנשבעין — דחזקה דאין שכיר משהה שכרו, ואין בעה"ב עובר בבל תלין; והכא הרי שהה שכיר, ובעה"ב עבר, דמודה שקצץ לו אחת ועדיין חייב לו. וליכא למימר דמיירי כגון דאמר "לא קצצתי לך אלא אחת, ופרעתי לך", דא"כ בזמנו אמאי נשבע ונוטל? הא כרבי יהודה מוקמי לה, ואיהו בעי הודאה במקצת. ואין לתרץ נמי כגון שאומר "אותה אחת שקצצתי לך, ברשותך השהיתי", דלא עבר בבל תלין — דמ"מ חזקה דאין שכיר משהה שכרו ליכא, דהרי שיהה אחת. ודוחק לומר דמאי דחזינן דשיהה — שיהה, ומאי דלא חזינן — דלא שיהה, לא שיהה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 45b:8:1.english: If he gave it to him within its time, he swears and collects - And if you ask: But didn't [the Gemara] say in the chapter "HaMekabel" (Bava Metzia 112b, there): [If] the craftsman says, "You agreed on two with me," and the other says, "I agreed with you on only one," the one who seeks to extract [payment] from his fellow bears the burden of proof, for the agreement on a price is something known! And in the chapter "Kol HaNishbain" (Shevuot 46a, there) [the Gemara] raises this difficulty against it, and answers: that this [Mishnah] here follows Rabbi Yehuda, [who holds] that he does not remember the agreed price either, since he is preoccupied with his workers. And if you ask: If so, [then] after its time as well, why did [the Gemara] say that the one who seeks to extract from his fellow bears the burden of proof? We should have said that he swears and collects! For what is the reason that we say elsewhere that after its time he does not swear and collect, as [the Gemara] explains at the beginning of "Kol HaNishbain" — because of the presumption that a hired worker does not delay [collecting] his wages, and a householder does not transgress "you shall not delay [payment]"; but here, the worker did delay, and the householder did transgress, since he admits that he agreed on one with him and still owes him! And one cannot say that [the Gemara] is speaking of a case where [the householder] says, "I agreed with you on only one, and I paid you," for if so, why within its time does he swear and collect? Surely we establish it according to Rabbi Yehuda, and he requires a partial admission. Nor can one answer [that it is] where he says, "That one that I agreed on with you, I delayed with your permission," so that he did not transgress "you shall not delay" — for in any case, the presumption that a hired worker does not delay his wages does not exist, since he did delay one. And it is a stretch to say that what we see that he delayed, he delayed, and what we do not see, [we say] that he did not delay, he did not delay.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 45b:9:1.hebrew: אי דאיכא עדים ליחזי עדים מאי קאמרי - דודאי ידעי הקציצה, דרגילות הוא. תימה לר"י: דעדיפא מינה הוה ליה למיפרך, דאי איכא עדים וראה, דאכתי לא מסיק אדעתיה לאוקמה בלא ראה, אם כן אמאי מהימן אומן שהטלית בידו? והכי הוה ליה למימר: בשלמא לרבא מוקי לה בדליכא עדים, דמהימן לרבא במיגו; אלא לאביי במאי מוקי לה? בין דאיכא עדים בין דליכא עדים לא מהימן במיגו. ויש לומר דהכי קאמר: אי דאיכא עדים — ואתא לאשמועינן דאע"ג דאיכא עדים אומן מהימן, וכגון דלא ראה — ליחזי עדים מאי קאמרי! אלא לאו דליכא עדים, דתו לא מצית לאוקומי בדלא ראה, דאם כן מאי קא משמע לן? פשיטא דכי ליכא עדים ולא ראה דמהימן, ואין כאן שום חידוש! אלא ודאי איירי בראה, ואפ"ה אומן מהימן. ומשני: לעולם בדליכא עדים ולא ראה, ולא תני לרישא לשום חידוש, אלא משום סיפא דבעי לאשמועינן דינא בנתנה לו, תנא נמי רישא כל זמן שהטלית ביד אומן, אע"ג דפשיטא היא. ואין להקשות, במאי דמשני אביי, אמאי נקט בסיפא "נתנה לו"? הוה ליה למיתני "ראהו בידו אע"פ שהטלית ביד אומן"! דהא לא נחת תנא לאשמועינן מידי בדינא דראה, ולהכי קתני "נתנה לו". והוא הדין דראה נמי כנתנה דמי, שהיה צריך ליתנה לו על כרחו:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 45b:9:1.english: "If there are witnesses, let us see what the witnesses say" - For they surely know the stipulated price, since it is customary [for witnesses to know it]. Rabbeinu Yitzchak (the Ri) was puzzled: [The Gemara] should have objected with something stronger than this. For if there are witnesses and he saw [the craftsman holding the garment] — since it has not yet occurred to [the Gemara] to establish it as a case where he did not see — then why is the craftsman believed when the garment is in his hand? And this is how it should have put it: Granted, according to Rava, who establishes it as a case where there are no witnesses, the craftsman is believed by virtue of a migo; but according to Abaye, in what case does he establish it? Whether there are witnesses or there are no witnesses, [the craftsman] is not believed on the basis of a migo. And one can say that this is what [the Gemara] is saying: If there are witnesses — and [the Mishnah] comes to teach us that even though there are witnesses, the craftsman is believed, and it is in a case where [the owner] did not see — then let us see what the witnesses say! Rather, is it not [a case] where there are no witnesses? [The Gemara answers that] one can no longer establish it as a case where he did not see, for if so, what is [the Mishnah] teaching us? It is obvious that when there are no witnesses and he did not see, [the craftsman] is believed, and there is no novelty here! Rather, it must certainly be speaking of a case where he saw, and nevertheless the craftsman is believed. And [Abaye] answers: Actually, it is a case where there are no witnesses and he did not see, and [the Tanna] did not teach the first clause for the sake of any novelty, but because of the latter clause, where he wished to teach us the law in the case where [the owner] gave it to him; [therefore] the Tanna also taught the first clause — "as long as the garment is in the craftsman's hand" — even though it is obvious. And one should not object, [regarding what Abaye answered]: Why did [the Tanna] state in the latter clause "he gave it to him"? He should have taught "he saw it in his hand, even though the garment is in the craftsman's hand"! [The answer is that] the Tanna did not set out to teach us anything about the law of "he saw," and therefore he taught "he gave it to him." And the same law applies where he saw, which is also considered like "he gave," for he would have had to give it to him in any case.
